facts.fact: Tom Doak and Jim Urbina, opened 2010, built on Charles Blair Macdonald's template holes; the 8th is the Biarritz.
The club's own marks are an M with crossed clubs in an O, and a 'ghost tree' cedar (both avoided).

current.subject: A tweed flat cap above a pipe, for C.B. Macdonald.
current.keep: The idea of the founder, suggested by his cap and pipe rather than a face.
current.weaknesses: Two separate objects stacked; the cap is flat and the tweed hardly shows.

concepts.name: The Founder's Cap
concepts.rationale: One lockup: a properly shaped tweed flat cap with a check you can see, the pipe laid across its band, a wisp of smoke.
references: C.B. Macdonald, whose templates the course follows (fact)
concepts.symbolism: The gentleman architect, present without a portrait.
concepts.typography: Playfair Display SC: high-contrast, Edwardian, Macdonald's era.
concepts.strengths: Characterful and specific to the course's homage.
concepts.tradeoffs: Busier than the best icons; the pipe is dated imagery.

concepts.name: The Biarritz
concepts.rationale: The 8th hole's green in section: front plateau, the deep swale, the pin on the back plateau, a ball on its way down. The template hole every architecture fan knows.
concepts.symbolism: The swale is the joke and the test: Old Mac's whole idea in one line.
concepts.strengths: Original and golf-literate; a simple graphic line.
concepts.tradeoffs: Needs golf literacy; at 1x it reads as a green valley rather than a named hole.

recommendation: Concept 1. It keeps the developer's homage to Macdonald and is the more recognisable object; the Biarritz is a lovely second mark for course guides.
